correspondence.component_scope: Southernmost opening and connector into the upper Tempati setting
correspondence.finding: The selected opening first turns west and north before entering the longer northward eastern headwater corridor. The national sketches and ministry figure are too generalized at this extreme southern start; the detailed project maps begin farther downstream or omit the full opening. Their coverage does not securely establish this complete initial feeder and connector.
correspondence.material_gap: Independent readable original cartography for the full southern opening through its connection into the mapped Tempati, rather than extrapolation from the downstream name or basin.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern headward course west of Merian toward Java
correspondence.finding: Sabajo Maps 1-1, 4.1-2 and 4.11-6 show the selected eastern course northward west of Merian, with the project-road crossing and successive bends continuing to Java. The western Little/Kleine Commewijne follows a different approach from the Sabajo side. These are distinct branches, not interchangeable names for the selected line.

correspondence.component_scope: Java junction and separate western tributaries
correspondence.finding: The eastern Tempati approach joins the western Kleine Commewijne near Java and continues north. A separate southwest approach joins farther down near the Gododrai sector; Holthuis labels the mapped western contribution Mapane. The selected line follows neither western headwater branch upstream.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward Commewijne trunk and Stolkertsijver transition setting
correspondence.finding: The northbound trunk passes the Pennenica sector and continues through the Stolkertsijver road-crossing setting. The ministry map and its station table directly identify Commewijne there. The two selected model pieces meet in this setting; the model boundary is not taken as a river-name boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern bend, Cottica junction and westward lower course
correspondence.finding: The selected route bends northwest, receives the separately mapped Cottica from the east, and follows the sinuous westward lower Commewijne. It does not turn east into Cottica, Moengo, Perica or the eastern coastal connections.

correspondence.component_scope: Terminal at the Suriname estuarine confluence
correspondence.finding: The final western reach enters the Suriname River estuarine setting beside Nieuw Amsterdam, north of Paramaribo. The 1999 water-resources profile expressly places the outfall in that estuary. Atlantic discharge is through the receiving Suriname system; the selected geometry is not asserted to include the remaining oceanward estuary.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake and reservoir separation
correspondence.finding: The national and project maps place Brokopondo reservoir on the separate Suriname River west of the selected Tempati–Commewijne corridor. No selected lake or reservoir passage is depicted within the covered route. No inference is made about the missing initial feeder from nearby reservoir or watershed membership.
correspondence.material_gap: Initial feeder remains outside the completed source correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: FID8819-opening-and-northwest-course
correspondence.finding: The selected opening is at the western Vildtland exposed-land/ice-margin setting. The northwest continuation leaves that margin and runs across the continental-ice and isolated-rock surroundings west of Vildtland and west of the Marie Sophie Gletscher corridor. The source distinguishes those land and ice areas; it does not show this entire initial modeled run as a named natural river.
correspondence.correspondence: read_in_original; no uninspected map or connector area
correspondence.name_scope: Vildtland names land and Marie Sophie Gletscher names a glacier. Neither is a river candidate. No surface-water or subglacial continuity is inferred from the selected model.
correspondence.correspondence_status: read_in_original; no uninspected map or connector area

correspondence.component_scope: FID8819-western-turn-and-northern-ice-margin-approach
correspondence.finding: The broad western turn and north/northeast continuation occupy the ice-margin and exposed-rock setting west and northwest of Inuiteq Sø. The original provides the complete surrounding ice and rock geography through this turn and into the belt below the Midsommersø valley.
correspondence.correspondence: read_in_original; no uninspected map or connector area
correspondence.name_scope: Inuiteq Sø is a separately mapped lake to the east/southeast of this turn. Proximity does not establish a selected lake traversal, outlet direction or named-river connection.
correspondence.correspondence_status: read_in_original; no uninspected map or connector area

correspondence.component_scope: FID8819-long-central-eastward-connection
correspondence.finding: The long central eastward component crosses the exposed-rock and Quaternary-covered belt north of Inuiteq Sø and south of the Midsommersø lake/valley system. Both ends and the intervening area are visible in the same original map. The selected straight generalized component is not treated as a surveyed river trace.
correspondence.correspondence: read_in_original; no uninspected map or connector area
correspondence.name_scope: The map supplies terrain coverage through this connection. It does not establish one named hydraulic link from the opening ice-margin setting through the rock/valley belt. No reservoir is identified.
correspondence.correspondence_status: read_in_original; no uninspected map or connector area

correspondence.component_scope: FID8819-central-northward-bend
correspondence.finding: The next northward bend passes through the Quaternary-covered valley belt south of the Midsommersø lakes, then approaches the eastern Nedre Midsommersø setting. The original shows the adjacent rock ridges, lake margins and valley branches throughout the bend.
correspondence.correspondence: read_in_original; no uninspected map or connector area
correspondence.name_scope: Øvre Midsommersø and Nedre Midsommersø retain lake feature scope. Their neighboring channels and the selected modeled line do not by themselves establish a common whole-route river name.
correspondence.correspondence_status: read_in_original; no uninspected map or connector area

correspondence.component_scope: FID8819-eastern-lake-and-wandel-valley-transition
correspondence.finding: This interval occupies the mapped eastern Nedre Midsommersø lake/shore setting and the valley leading east toward Wandel Dal. The original exposes the lake-to-valley transition, surrounding Quaternary cover and the nearby valley branches. No missing cartographic panel is involved.
correspondence.correspondence: read_in_original; no uninspected map or connector area
correspondence.name_scope: The eastern lake setting and downstream valley are read as distinct geographic components. The review does not assert that all selected segments, lakes or nearby branch valleys are one continuous surface or subglacial river.
correspondence.correspondence_status: read_in_original; no uninspected map or connector area

correspondence.component_scope: FID8819-wandel-dal-and-fjord-terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selected corridor continues through the Wandel Dal setting and into the area shown as Jørgen Brønlund Fjord. The terminal is in the mapped fjord water/shore setting west of Kap Harald Moltke, on the branch leading toward Independence Fjord. The original distinguishes the valley, fjord, adjoining rock and sediment-covered shores, and receiving fjord geography.
correspondence.correspondence: read_in_original; no uninspected map or connector area
correspondence.name_scope: The retained sea terminal classification is model metadata. The ending is not established as an ordinary natural-river mouth: part of the selected lower setting is mapped as fjord. Jørgen Brønlund Fjord, Independence Fjord and Wandel Dal are contextual feature names, not candidate names for the whole modeled river group.
correspondence.correspondence_status: read_in_original; no uninspected map or connector area

correspondence.component_scope: Selected northwestern opening and first named corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected opening is the small southeastward stream on the San Ernesto/Puntas del Gualeguaychú side, west of the Arroyo Barú setting. Original stream linework depicts its entry into the eastward Gualeguaychú corridor. The map labels the ensuing corridor Gualeguaychú. The small initial feeder is not independently named by this reading, and the settlement name Puntas del Gualeguaychú is not used as a hydronym.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at generalized corridor/junction scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper and upper-middle southward corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected course turns south beside Arroyo Barú and La Clarita, then southwest past Pueblo Cazes/Colonia Vázquez and west of Villa Elisa. The original river line and junction setting correspond throughout at ordinary corridor scale. Nearby streams, roads and settlement labels are distinguished from the selected Gualeguaychú channel.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at generalized corridor/junction scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle corridor toward Caseros and the southern lowlands
correspondence.finding: The river continues through the Crucecita Grande/San Pedro-side lowlands, passes west of Pronunciamiento and across the road/rail corridor west of Caseros, then continues south east of the Aldea San Antonio/Urdinarrain side. The retained selection follows the mapped main tributary-river corridor through these junctions, rather than transferring to the separate Uruguay River farther east. Minor sheet seams do not obscure a material branch-choice or connector at this generalized scale.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at generalized corridor/junction scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Gualeguaychú and city approach
correspondence.finding: The selected southern approach follows the Gualeguaychú corridor past the Salto Grande/Salto Chico and Puerto del Tala settings toward Gualeguaychú city. Those mapped local feature labels are not construed as separate reservoirs or names of the whole selected route. The 1:100,000 original depicts the river and adjoining floodplain continuously through the lower city approach omitted by the 250k white seam. The separately named Gualeyán joins from the west and is not the selected upstream corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at generalized corridor/junction scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward lower bends and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: Below Gualeguaychú city, the selected continuation follows the broad river south and then east through the lower bends to Río Uruguay beside Isla Lorenzo. The map depicts surrounding floodplain channels and the distinct receiving river. The chosen route is the Gualeguaychú tributary entering Río Uruguay. It is not the Uruguay mainstem, an ocean mouth, or a basis for renaming nearby El Cura, Capilla or Bellaco channels. The retained terminal class sea is model metadata only. The actual geographical terminal is the Gualeguaychú–Uruguay river junction.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at generalized corridor/junction scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern opening and initial northward-to-northwestward feeder
correspondence.finding: The selected model opens inland and bends north/northwest. This direction is model orientation only. The retained reserve map shows the wider Kakiattuq, Descareaux and Qullinaaraaluk lake region; the geological report places the study north of Lac Minto. Neither original distinguishes the selected small opening and its first lake/stream transfers. No nearby lake label is treated as the selected source.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper westward corridor and successive waterbody passages
correspondence.finding: Regional cartography depicts dense lakes and streams between the separately labelled northern drainage and Boniface corridor. It does not resolve each selected lake entrance, outlet and intervening feeder at ordinary component scale. The geological report Figure2 omits most of this smaller hydrography. No named-lake traversal or continuous river identity is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Central westward continuation and joining relations
correspondence.finding: The original regional maps show that this is a lake-rich, branching inland hydrographic landscape, with distinct neighbouring river corridors. The exact selected westward chain and the relationships at its material joins cannot be distinguished confidently from those generalized views. Model connectivity alone is not evidence that the source map links these reaches.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestward lower-interior corridor
correspondence.finding: The retained regional originals show a coastal-facing drainage network between the Boniface and Qikirtaluup Kuunga settings. They do not independently establish the entire selected northwestward route or the branch chosen at every material junction. Neither regional label is assigned to this selected portion.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern bend, western continuation and lower channel connections
correspondence.finding: The selected model turns north and then west before the coast. That orientation is retained metadata only. The reserve and CEHQ maps depict adjacent coastal-facing waterways, but the actual selected bend, lake/channel links and joining relations remain unresolved in the available original cartography.

correspondence.component_scope: Final coastal approach and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: Both retained regional originals identify the Hudson Bay coast and distinguish the coastal Qikirtaluup Kuunga and more southerly Boniface settings. They do not independently resolve the selected final channel, whether its last passage belongs to a river or coastal embayment, and its actual receiving-water connection. The selected sea terminal classification is model metadata; a nearby river or bay label is not accepted as correspondence.
